description: Shared Renovate policy for every ralton-dev and bralton repo.
A repo opts in with `"extends": ["github>ralton-dev/.github"]` and keeps only its own grouping rules and dashboard title.

packageRules.description: Routine minor, patch, digest and pin updates go in one weekly PR that merges itself once CI is green.
A minor bump of a 0.x package may be breaking, so it gets its own PR and a manual merge, like a major.

Major updates open as PRs without dashboard approval, and wait for a manual merge. No groupName here: this rule runs after the presets above, and clearing the group would undo the Node.js runtime grouping.

Major updates of GitHub Actions go in one PR per repo, still labelled and merged by hand through the rule above. Only `uses: owner/repo@ref` action references match: runner images, container images and the Node or tool versions passed to setup actions keep their own PRs and groups.

Move every Python pin in a repo to a new feature release (3.x to 3.y) in one PR, merged by hand like a Node major. Renovate calls 3.12 to 3.15 a minor, so without this it rides in the routine PR and merges itself. Matches requires-python, .python-version, `python` images, setup-python, and asdf, mise and Poetry pins. Patch releases stay routine. This lives here, not in runtimes.json, because it must run after the routine rule, which would otherwise take the minor back.

An override key scoped to a version line or a parent (`name@1`, `parent>child`) pins what that line or parent gets, so moving its value to a new major hands the new major to packages written for the old one. Drop those updates. Updates inside the line still arrive, and a bare-name override still gets its majors.
The same for a 0.x minor on a scoped override key, which may be breaking, as the 0.x rule above treats it.

Hold TypeScript below 7 in a repo that is below 7. typescript-eslint does not support TypeScript 7 and fails, and dependency-cruiser supports only <7 and under 7 cruises no modules, so its check passes while checking nothing. TypeScript 7 also removes `baseUrl`. A repo already on 7 keeps its 7.x updates. Remove this rule once typescript-eslint and dependency-cruiser both release TypeScript 7 support. The current version is a regex on the major, because a regex is checked against the locked version or, when Renovate finds none (an npm workspace package whose TypeScript is hoisted to the root), the declared range; a version range here is checked against the locked version only and would not match.
